accessibility.textAlternative: How a seed library works. A seed library is a shared collection of seeds for planting. In this invented school example, families contribute in several ways. Some donate seeds; others clean storage tins or teach pupils when to plant. No family must pay money to take part. Pupils label each tin with the seed type and record each loan. The record helps the group know what is available. Borrowers return some seeds after their harvest so the collection can be used again. As a result, more pupils can borrow seeds in the next planting season. Dry storage helps protect the collection. Damp seeds may develop mould and become unsuitable for planting. Pupils inspect the tins each week and keep them in a dry cupboard. This example explains a possible system; it does not report measured results from a real school.
